whatis.intro: Inventory turnover counts how many times a year the stock on your floor is sold and bought again. It measures the speed of the shelf, not the size of it. At this calculator's defaults, the shelf empties and refills 12.0 times a year.

cards.title: Speed, with costly lines weighing most
cards.body: Speed, weighted by dollars. Every line feeds the same 12.0 turns, and the lines holding the most cost pull it hardest.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for speed weighted by the dollars on each line

cards.title: Fast is not the same as profitable
cards.body: Profit. A line can turn fast and earn little, or turn slowly at a margin worth waiting for. Turns say how fast, not how well.
cards.alt: Minus sign, for the margin turns do not measure

cards.title: Lines held for one account
cards.body: Items you stock for a single customer turn at that customer's pace. When that customer stops ordering one, the stock stops moving and still sits inside the average.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for lines stocked for a single account

who.intro: Finance leads, buyers and owners at independent distributors use it to ask one question: how hard is the stock working? It helps them set turn targets and spot cash sitting still.

look.h2: What can skew an inventory turnover ratio
look.intro: Turns come from one division, and the division never fails. The two numbers you divide are where the ratio drifts, so look here before setting a target.

steps.title: The same twelve months on both sides
steps.body: Cost of goods and average inventory have to cover the same period. Pair a calendar year of sales with a fiscal year of stock and the ratio measures neither year.

steps.title: Sales that never touched the shelf
steps.body: Drop shipped and cross docked product lands in cost of goods without sitting in stock. Leave it in and 12.0 turns reads faster than your shelf moves.

steps.title: Write offs that flatter the ratio
steps.body: Writing off dead stock lowers average inventory without selling a single case. Turns go up, and nothing moved any faster.

vos.h2: Where VOS sits next to your turns
vos.h3: Every turn starts with an account's order
vos.body: VOS does not calculate your turns or keep your books. It handles the order that takes stock off the shelf: customers speak it into the VOS app and review each line first.
